articles.title: Israeli Officials Accused of Genocide in Gaza
articles.summary: Amnesty International has called on the International Criminal Court (ICC) to investigate allegations of genocide by Israeli officials against women and newborns in Gaza, citing severe impacts on reproductive health.
articles.content: Amnesty International has called on the International Criminal Court (ICC) to launch an investigation into allegations of genocide by Israeli officials against women and newborns in Gaza. The rights group's concerns centre around measures taken by Israel that it claims have severely impacted reproductive health in the region. These measures include blocking access to fertility treatment, leading to a significant increase in pregnancy complications such as miscarriage and stillbirth. A report published on Wednesday highlights the devastating effects of the war on women's physical, mental, and reproductive well-being in Gaza since October 2023. The report notes that Israel's actions have contributed to an alarming rise in birth-related complications during this period. Amnesty International Secretary General Agnès Callamard expressed serious concerns about the intentional nature of these measures at a press conference on Wednesday. The Israeli defence ministry's response to Amnesty International's report has been swift, accusing the organization of spreading false narratives on behalf of Hamas. In a statement, COGAT claimed that over 27,000 tonnes of medical equipment and supplies have entered Gaza since the US-brokered ceasefire in October 2025, with 35 hospitals operating, including facilities dedicated to women's health and fertility. Despite these assertions, Amnesty International's report paints a starkly different picture, detailing cases where women and girls were killed or injured while seeking medical care or giving birth in maternity wards in Gaza under intense bombardment. Women who suffered injuries during pregnancy or childbirth often continued to care for their newborns, highlighting the extreme difficulties faced by families in Gaza due to ongoing shortages of essential medical supplies. The Israeli military's actions in Gaza have been scrutinized for their potential impact on birth rates within the Palestinian population. In a recent report, human rights organization Amnesty International highlighted two incidents where paramedics were fired upon while attempting to transport women about to give birth across the Yellow Line demarcating the area under Israeli control. According to eyewitness accounts, both incidents occurred just a few hundred meters from this boundary in early 2026. The testimonies of the paramedics provide disturbing evidence of the risks faced by pregnant women and their families in Gaza. The report also documents the tragic case of a newborn infant who died after contracting an infection while sharing an incubator with another sick baby, further underscoring the dire situation facing medical facilities in the region. Gaza's health ministry, which operates under Hamas, has recorded over 74,000 Palestinian fatalities since the outbreak of war sparked by Hamas's October 7, 2023 attack. The UN considers these figures reliable due to their impartial nature. The ongoing conflict has put an immense strain on medical services in Gaza, leaving families struggling to access even basic care for themselves and their newborns. This is reflected in the testimonies of women who have suffered injuries during pregnancy or childbirth but continue to care for their infants despite these challenges. Amnesty International's report raises concerns about Israel's actions in Gaza and whether they constitute a form of genocide, as defined by Article II of the UN Convention on the Prevention and Punishment of the Crime of Genocide. A significant decline has been reported in live births in Gaza for the first half of 2025 compared to the same period two years prior, with a drop of approximately 41 percent. This trend is also reflected in UN records, which show a decrease in deliveries during the first six months of 2026 compared to the previous year. The investigation by Amnesty International has uncovered evidence of Palestinian armed groups using hospitals for various purposes, including holding hostages and torturing Palestinians. Conversely, there is no supporting evidence to corroborate Israeli claims that these medical facilities are being utilized as command centers for Hamas. Amnesty's findings also reveal a stark contrast in reproductive healthcare services available in Gaza before the war, with at least nine clinics offering IVF treatments, but none currently providing this service. As a result, thousands of stored embryos, sperm, and eggs were destroyed, highlighting the devastating impact on the population's access to essential medical care. articles.title: Tidal Bans Fully AI-Generated Music from December 9
articles.summary: Tidal has announced it will no longer accept or host fully AI-generated music tracks on its platform.
articles.content: Tidal has made a bold move to combat an influx of music generated entirely by artificial intelligence (AI). The music streaming app announced on Tuesday that it will no longer accept or host tracks that are 100% AI-generated. As the company struggles to keep up with the sheer volume of non-human music, Tidal's decision aims to stem the tide. According to internal data, a staggering 43% of tracks distributed to the platform over the past three months were found to be entirely AI-generated. This issue has been exacerbated by distributors such as DistroKid and TuneCore, which have also been submitting large quantities of AI music for upload. Tidal had previously tried to mitigate the problem by labeling and demonetizing affected tracks, but it seems this approach was insufficient. As a result, Tidal will start rejecting all fully AI-generated tracks from December 9 onwards. This move is expected to affect not just the individual tracks themselves, but also the royalty pool, which distributes subscription and ad revenue to rights holders who own the music. Tidal's efforts to safeguard its artist community have led to a significant milestone, with over 65,000 tracks removed from the platform due to concerns of artist-name impersonation. The company has implemented strict measures to prevent AI-generated music from flooding the site, citing that such content "diverts streams and royalties away from the artists" and can confuse fans. In a statement, Tidal emphasized its commitment to supporting authentic music and artists, stating that the authentic music and artists... get buried when AI-generated tracks dominate. To ensure compliance with these new guidelines, Tidal uses Ircam Amplify to detect AI-generated content. While some assistance from AI is permitted, tracks where the creator used AI but did not rely on it for the entire composition will still be allowed, the company has yet to specify exactly how much AI help will be tolerated. The ease with which music can now be generated using online tools, such as Suno and Google's Lyria, highlights the need for platforms like Tidal to take a firm stance against AI-generated content. These tools allow users to create songs using text prompts or even images, raising questions about authorship and ownership in the digital age. The rise of artificial intelligence in music production has led to a new challenge for streaming services: how to distinguish between human-created content and its machine-made counterpart. While it's not against the law to generate AI music and distribute it through various platforms, there are strict guidelines that creators must follow to avoid copyright infringement and other issues. In particular, AI-generated music cannot be made to sound like a specific artist or mimic their style without permission. This means that if an AI tool is used to create a song in the style of a well-known musician, it cannot be released under that artist's name or likeness. As a result, streaming apps are taking steps to differentiate between human and AI-created content, with some platforms providing tools for listeners to identify which tracks were generated by machines. articles.title: Apple Watch Navigation Feature Wins Over Drivers with Haptic Feedback
articles.summary: A game-changing feature on Apple Watch has provided haptic feedback during navigation for many drivers who swear by its convenience.
articles.content: A game-changing feature on Apple Watch has won over many drivers who swear by its convenience. For those deeply invested in the Apple ecosystem, the choice between using Apple Maps or Google Maps is no longer as straightforward as it once was. Apple's decision to overhaul its maps app after a series of inaccuracies led to safety concerns has paid off, with many users now reporting little difference between the two options when used for navigation. One user recently undertook a long drive across the country and found Apple Maps to be the better choice for their needs. The key advantage of using Apple Watch in conjunction with CarPlay lies in its ability to provide haptic feedback, which can be particularly useful during extended periods behind the wheel. When using Apple Watch in conjunction with CarPlay, one of the key advantages lies in its ability to provide clear visual and audio alerts that coincide with haptic feedback on your wrist. These vibrations are particularly useful during extended periods behind the wheel, as they tap your wrist whenever a turn is imminent, ensuring you stay focused on the road. The different vibration patterns for left and right turns make it virtually impossible to miss a turnoff, which could be lifesaving if you're prone to nodding off on long drives. To verify that haptic feedback is active or disable it, open the Watch app on your iPhone, select the My Watch tab, then go to Apps , followed by Maps . From there, you can toggle alerts for various activities, including Driving with CarPlay, walking, and cycling. Leaving cycling alerts on may be a good idea, as Apple Maps can provide useful information while riding a bike or personal electric vehicle like a scooter or unicycle. In such situations, audio and haptic cues are often the only practical way to make turns safely without taking your eyes off the road. The limitations of running CarPlay exclusively from an Apple Watch have become clear. Even the most powerful watch model, the Ultra 4, lacks the necessary processing power to handle such a demanding feature. As a result, using CarPlay on an Apple Watch would be extremely taxing on its battery life. One feature that does work seamlessly with Apple CarPlay is the ability to get driving directions directly from the watchOS version of Apple Maps. This allows users to receive haptic and audio cues while keeping their eyes on the road, making navigation safer and more convenient. However, this requires a nearby iPhone to function properly. Users who do not have access to their iPhone can still download offline maps or use an Apple Watch with an active cellular plan. But it's worth noting that many carriers charge extra for smartwatch coverage, which may not be a worthwhile investment if the user rarely uses both phone and watch data simultaneously. In summary, while some features of CarPlay do work on an Apple Watch, its limitations remain significant, particularly when it comes to running the feature exclusively. Lauren Bis, who described his decision to self-deport as a significant victory for the Trump administration's immigration policies. Lauren Bis's words of celebration notwithstanding, a complex situation unfolded in Maryland as Kilmar Abrego Garcia prepared to leave the United States for Spain. Court records had yet to reflect an order ending proceedings against him, despite an agreement being reached that would pave the way for his departure. Sealed filings in his civil case against the administration over the past few weeks suggested a behind-the-scenes effort was underway. Garcia's story is one of a life spent living and working in Maryland under regular supervision by Immigration and Customs Enforcement. He had entered the country illegally as a teenager but had built a life here, marrying an American citizen and having a child with her. An immigration judge's 2019 ruling that he could not be deported to El Salvador due to safety concerns from gang members seemed to have been ignored. The alleged abuses at CECOT megaprison in El Salvador, where Garcia was sent after his deportation, had been decried by activists who described inmates being packed into cells with no time outdoors. Following his deportation to El Salvador, Kilmar Abrego Garcia's case continued to unfold as he sought to return to a country of his choice, rather than Liberia as proposed by the Department of Homeland Security. Court records showed that Abrego Garcia had expressed a desire to go to Costa Rica, which sparked a dispute with immigration officials who were pushing for his removal to Liberia. The authorities' decision was met with resistance from Abrego Garcia, who continued to fight deportation through an ongoing lawsuit. The government's appeal of the initial decision not to pursue charges in Tennessee after a 2022 traffic stop added another layer of complexity to Abrego Garcia's case, as he also faced allegations that he was an MS-13 gang member, which he strongly denied. In addition to the allegations related to his involvement with MS-13, he also faced scrutiny over a 2022 traffic stop where police made an assessment based on his clothing and tattoos, as well as information from a confidential informant. District Judge Waverly Crenshaw had previously expressed concerns about statements made by top Trump administration officials regarding Abrego Garcia's case, warning that they were "exaggerated if not simply inaccurate" and could potentially sway a jury. articles.summary: A New York jury has delivered a verdict in a high-profile trial against Chinese tech giant Huawei, finding the company guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offenses.
articles.content: A New York jury has delivered a verdict in a high-profile trial against Chinese tech giant Huawei, finding the company guilty of stealing trade secrets and other criminal offenses. The acquittal on racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice charges is a significant development in the ongoing case. The lengthy trial, which concluded after three months, highlights US concerns about Huawei's operations. Huawei has been at the center of a global debate over national security threats, with the Trump administration leading efforts to curb its influence. Allegations have surfaced that Huawei could be spying on behalf of the Chinese government, sparking fears among countries worldwide. The US has urged nations not to use Huawei infrastructure for new 5G mobile network rollouts. The Department of Justice revealed that jurors found Huawei guilty of 10 out of 12 counts, including bank fraud and conspiracy to defraud the United States. This development raises questions about the extent to which Huawei's business practices align with US laws. The acquittal on more serious charges may be seen as a partial victory for the company. The verdict marks another chapter in the ongoing saga surrounding Huawei's operations in the US. As concerns over national security and trade secrets continue, it remains to be seen how this decision will impact Huawei's future dealings with American companies and entities. The verdict marks a significant development in the ongoing saga surrounding Huawei's business practices. Huawei and three of its subsidiaries have been found guilty of stealing trade secrets from American companies, a serious offense that has far-reaching implications for the Chinese tech giant. Despite this conviction, Huawei was acquitted on two other charges: racketeering conspiracy and obstruction of justice. The company has welcomed this outcome, stating that it confirms their allegations were baseless and vindicates their long-held position over the past eight years. The jury's decision to convict Huawei on trade secrets charges is a major blow to the company's reputation, particularly given the severity of the offense involved. The indictment alleged that Huawei's data collection efforts allowed it to develop products similar to those of its competitors, which were then sold at lower prices, giving the company an unfair advantage in the market. Prosecutors claimed that this information was obtained through various means, including the attempted recruitment of employees from US telecoms firms and the misappropriation of intellectual property such as source code, user manuals for internet routers, and technical specifications for antennas and robots. Assistant Attorney General Tysen A. Duva stated that the verdict sends a clear message about America's commitment to defending its businesses and workers against foreign corporations that engage in unfair practices, including theft and deception. articles.title: Bob Woodward Reveals Sources in New Memoir
articles.summary: Veteran journalist Bob Woodward has spent decades exposing secrets from Washington's corridors of power. In his new memoir "Secrets, he reveals some of the secrets about himself, shedding...
articles.content: Veteran journalist Bob Woodward has spent decades exposing secrets from Washington's corridors of power. In his new memoir "Secrets, he reveals some of the secrets about himself, shedding light on the anonymous sources that gave him unparalleled access to ten American presidents. Woodward sat down with Amna Nawaz and explained why he chose to name some of these sources in his book. According to Woodward, those who are still alive have given him permission to reveal their identities, while others have passed away, making it a matter of historical record. Additionally, many of the documents and records from these individuals are already publicly available. The decision to name these sources marks a significant departure for Woodward, whose Watergate coverage was made possible by information from President Nixon's own lawyers. This revelation is just one part of his memoir, which aims to provide more context to the historical record. By naming his sources, Woodward hopes to add depth and clarity to our understanding of some of America's most pivotal moments. Woodward's decision to name these sources has sparked curiosity about why he chose this moment to reveal their identities. He believes that with many of these individuals deceased or having given him permission, it is now part of history, and the time is right for more information to be shared. In his new book Secrets, Bob Woodward reveals why he's naming sources from decades past, including those who were involved in the Nixon administration. He starts by mentioning two individuals - Len Garment and Fred Buzhardt - who initially wanted to remain anonymous but eventually agreed to share their information with him. Woodward recalls that these individuals had a unique opportunity to listen to many of the infamous Nixon tapes, which exposed the former president's deceitful nature. As they delved deeper into the recordings, they realized just how far-reaching Nixon's lies and deceptions went, ultimately leading them to cooperate with Woodward on his investigation. Their willingness to share their knowledge is all the more remarkable given that even some of Nixon's own lawyers had begun to doubt his integrity. One of these lawyers referred to Nixon as having a tainted mind, implying that his president's actions were driven by a flawed perception of reality. This candid assessment highlights the extent to which those closest to Nixon began to see him in a different light. Woodward's discussion with Amna Nawaz touches on a particularly poignant example of a source who was eager to share information but ultimately became disillusioned with Woodward's handling of their story. The individual, Dick Darman, was described as a dream source due to his enthusiasm for speaking out, but their friendship with Woodward came to an end after some of the details he provided were published in a subsequent report. Woodward explains that he chose to include this story because it underscores the complexities of working with sources who are often motivated by a desire to see justice served. As someone who has built his career on uncovering secrets, Woodward recognizes that sharing these stories can be both a privilege and a responsibility - one that requires careful consideration of the consequences for all parties involved. Woodward's decision to name some of his sources in Secrets is rooted in his understanding that many of them are now deceased or have given him permission to share their stories. This newfound openness has allowed Woodward to provide a more complete picture of events, one that sheds light on both the triumphs and failures of those who came before him. The story of Dick Darman serves as a reminder that even the most well-intentioned sources can become disillusioned with the way their information is used. As someone who has worked closely with many such individuals, Woodward understands the delicate balance between protecting sources' identities and sharing their stories in a responsible manner. Woodward's book Secrets offers a nuanced exploration of the challenges faced by journalists when working with sensitive information. By naming some of his sources, he aims to provide a more accurate account of historical events while also acknowledging the complexities involved in gathering and sharing such knowledge. Amidst the many stories shared in Secrets, Woodward's discussion with Amna Nawaz highlights the importance of considering the long-term consequences of one's actions. By including the story of Dick Darman, he underscores the need for journalists to be mindful not only of their sources' identities but also of the potential fallout from sharing sensitive information. Bob Woodward's new book Secrets is not just about his reporting career spanning over five decades, but also about his personal experiences and reflections on being a journalist. As he recounts in the book, Woodward was always mindful of the world around him, often finding himself in situations where nothing was truly off the record. He attributes this to his early life, where he developed a natural skepticism towards people and events from the age of 8. Woodward's approach to journalism is characterized by a deep understanding of human nature, which sometimes led to close relationships with sources. However, these connections also posed risks, as Woodward himself acknowledges in the book - a tension that he struggled to navigate throughout his career. In writing Secrets, Woodward has chosen to reveal more about himself and his experiences, describing it as a liberating experience. He shares personal anecdotes from his childhood, including traumatic events that shaped who he is today, and believes that this openness helps readers understand the journalist behind the stories. As Woodward shares intimate details about his personal life, it becomes clear that these experiences have had a profound impact on his worldview and approach to journalism. His childhood was marked by significant upheaval, including discovering at a young age that his parents were getting divorced - a revelation he stumbled upon while rummaging through his father's sock drawer and finding letters addressed to him. This event, combined with the trauma of a devastating fire in their family home, has left an indelible mark on Woodward. Even today, he still takes precautions against fires, keeping numerous extinguishers on hand as a reminder of that harrowing experience. These formative events have shaped Woodward's perspective, making him a catastrophic thinker who always considers the potential worst-case scenario. This mindset has influenced his work, particularly in his reporting on the presidency and the concentration of power. In covering high-stakes stories like the presidency, Woodward is acutely aware of the dangers that can arise when power is concentrated in one individual's hands. He points to the current president's actions as an example, citing the administration's handling of foreign policy and military interventions. The power dynamics at play within the presidency have raised concerns about the potential for abuse of authority. The current administration's handling of foreign policy and military interventions has drawn parallels to the Nixon era. This trend is particularly alarming given the president's ability to wield immense influence over domestic and international affairs. Woodward notes that this concentration of power is a hallmark of authoritarian regimes, not democracies. He points out that the president's actions often appear to be guided by personal whims rather than constitutional constraints. This raises questions about the limits of presidential authority and whether they can be checked by other branches of government. In recent interviews, Woodward observed that the president has consistently demonstrated a willingness to disregard established norms and protocols. His assertion that I do what I want is a stark reminder of the dangers of unchecked power. The implications of this mindset are far-reaching, with potential consequences for both domestic stability and global security. The president's actions have been characterized as tyrannical behavior by some observers. This label suggests that he may be disregarding fundamental principles of democracy in favor of personal agendas. Critics argue that the concentration of power in the presidency has created an environment in which individual interests can take precedence over the common good. Woodward's concerns about the president's impact on democracy are shared by many experts and analysts. They warn that the erosion of institutional checks and balances could have severe consequences for the health of democratic systems worldwide. The erosion of institutional checks and balances on executive power has been a gradual process, one that spans centuries. Looking back to the country's founding fathers provides valuable insight into the intentions behind these restraints. They were designed to prevent the concentration of power in the hands of any single individual or entity. The absence of these restraints today is a stark contrast to the original vision for the country. The forefathers would likely be shocked by the current state of affairs, and many would question what has happened to the principles they fought so hard to establish. As an award-winning journalist with over 50 years of experience covering every administration, Bob Woodward's perspective on this issue is particularly noteworthy. He emphasizes the importance of restraint in executive power, highlighting the dangers that arise when such limitations are absent. In his latest book, Secrets," Woodward imparts valuable advice to young journalists: work tirelessly and be persistent in seeking information from those in positions of power, always telegraphing a need for assistance and being pleasantly insistent.
